title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: What separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow never calls a language model, but an agent always does
In a workflow, code fixes the steps ahead of time; in an agent, the model chooses them
A workflow handles one request at a time, but an agent handles many at once
In a workflow, the model chooses the steps; in an agent, code fixes their order

items.stem: Which of these makerspace assistant designs is an agent?

options.text: Code always runs check_calendar, then book_slot, then sends a fixed confirmation text
Code sorts each question by keyword, then sends it to either the manual search or the calendar
Code runs three prompts in a fixed order, and each model reply is pasted into the next prompt
The model is given three tools and picks which to call, in what order, and when to stop

items.stem: Students send open-ended questions about a broken machine. What to look up next depends on what each earlier lookup returns, and no fixed sequence covers them. Which design fits this part of the assistant?

options.text: An agent, because the model must choose each next lookup from the results so far
A fixed workflow, because a workflow is always cheaper than an agent
A fixed workflow, because code can run the same lookups for every question
An agent, because an agent is always more reliable than a workflow

items.stem: A teammate says: "Booking a machine always goes check the calendar, reserve the slot, send a confirmation, so let's build it as an agent." Given a small model budget, what is the best reply?

options.text: Agree: an agent handles these steps more reliably because it reasons about each one
Agree: an agent costs less here, because it only calls the tools it needs
Disagree: the steps are the same every time, so a workflow has predictable cost and is easier to test
Disagree: a workflow cannot call tools, so it could not check the calendar or reserve

items.stem: A student question needs the calendar, the manuals and the training record. As an agent, the model requests those three tools one at a time and then writes its final answer, and each model call ends with one tool request or the final answer. A fixed workflow handles the same kind of question with exactly 2 model calls every time. Across 50 such questions, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow, in total?

A program asks the model to draft a booking confirmation. Code then checks that the machine and date match the booking. If they do not, the code asks the model to draft again, up to 3 drafts in total, and then stops with an error. Is this a workflow or an agent?

options.text: An agent, because it keeps looping until the result is right
A workflow, because the code sets the retry rule and limit; the model only writes text
An agent, because it makes more than one model call for a single request
A workflow only if it never retries; once it retries, the model is steering
